title: Albatros D.Va (IL-2)

sources.title: JoyPro cockpit catalog (from the IL-2 and real aircraft manuals)

intro: The Albatros D.Va was a German biplane fighter of the First World War. The cockpit is open in the oval plywood fuselage; the right hand flies and the left also works the throttle on the control column. The pilot has no mixture control.

areas.name: Gun breeches and sights
areas.text: The two machine guns and their sights sit right in front of the pilot.

panels.name: Gun breeches and sights
panels.text: These are the rear ends of the two machine guns and the sights between them.
panels.context: The pilot clears jams with the charging handles and aims with the sights.

controls.name: Left Spandau breech
controls.text: This is the rear end of the left machine gun, the breech, with a charging handle. The pilot cocks the gun with the handle and uses it to clear a jam.
controls.context: The guns sit right in front of the pilot. The pilot fires them with the triggers on the stick.

controls.name: Right Spandau breech
controls.text: This is the rear end of the right machine gun, the breech, with a charging handle. The pilot cocks the gun with the handle. This copy sits in the panel “Gun breeches and sights”.
controls.context: The guns sit right in front of the pilot. The pilot fires them with the triggers on the stick. This copy belongs to the panel “Gun breeches and sights”.

controls.name: Ring-and-bead sight
controls.text: This is a simple open sight between the guns: a ring at the rear and a bead at the front. The pilot lines up the bead in the ring with the target to aim.
controls.context: It is how First World War pilots aimed before reflector sights existed.

controls.name: Oigee optical sight (when fitted)
controls.text: This is a tube sight between the guns. It is fitted in some planes. The pilot looks through it to aim at the target.
controls.context: It is an alternative to the ring-and-bead sight between the guns.

areas.name: Instruments
areas.text: The few instruments of a First World War fighter sit on the panel.

panels.name: Instruments
panels.text: These are the few instruments: engine speed, height, fuel, fuel pressure, water temperature and the ignition switch.
panels.context: The pilot glances at them to keep the engine healthy.

controls.name: Tachometer
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the engine turns, in revolutions per minute (RPM).
controls.context: The pilot watches it all the time to keep the engine in its safe range.

controls.name: Altimeter
controls.text: This dial shows how high the plane is, measured from the air pressure. The needles work like the hands of a clock, one for the hundreds and one for the thousands of metres.
controls.context: The pilot checks it to stay clear of the ground and to hold the height the mission needs.

controls.name: Fuel gauge
controls.text: This dial shows how much fuel is left in the main tank.
controls.context: The pilot checks it to know how long the plane can still fly.

controls.name: Fuel pressure gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the pressure of the fuel. In the First World War planes it shows the pressure in the fuel tank that pushes the fuel to the engine.
controls.context: If the pressure drops, the pilot pumps it up again with the hand pump.

controls.name: Water temperature gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the temperature of the cooling water of the engine. The radiator cools the water.
controls.context: A rising temperature warns of overheating. The pilot can open the radiator shutters if the plane has them.

controls.name: Magneto (ignition) switch
controls.text: This switch turns the ignition of the engine on and off. The ignition makes the sparks that set the fuel alight.
controls.context: The pilot switches it on for the start. Switching it off stops the engine.

areas.name: Left quadrant
areas.text: The spark advance lever and the fuel controls are on the left.

panels.name: Left quadrant
panels.text: This is the small quadrant on the left with the spark advance lever, the fuel cock and the fuel pressure hand pump.
panels.context: The pilot works the fuel controls before the start.

controls.name: Spark advance lever
controls.text: This lever sets the ignition timing, when the sparks are made in the engine. The catalog calls it a spark advance lever.
controls.context: It sits in the small quadrant on the left of the cockpit, next to the fuel controls.

controls.name: Fuel cock
controls.text: This selector is the tap in the fuel line. It decides which tank feeds the engine. The catalog names the choice main or gravity tank for the First World War planes.
controls.context: The pilot opens it before starting and switches tanks when one runs dry.

controls.name: Fuel pressure hand pump
controls.text: This handle is a hand pump. Moving it builds up pressure in the fuel tank, which pushes the fuel to the engine.
controls.context: The pilot pumps it before the start and again if the fuel pressure gauge shows too little.

areas.name: Stick and throttle
areas.text: These are the controls on the pilot's stick or yoke and on the left-hand throttle side that JoyPro can assign to a joystick or throttle.

panels.name: Control stick
panels.text: This is the control stick and the buttons on its grip.
panels.context: The pilot flies with it and fires and drops the weapons from it.

controls.name: Left gun trigger
controls.text: This button on the stick grip is pressed with the thumb. It fires the plane's cannons, the heavier guns. In the game: press: Fire the left Spandau.
controls.context: Cannons hit harder than machine guns. The pilot uses them for the decisive burst on a target.

controls.name: Right gun trigger
controls.text: This is a second thumb trigger on the stick grip. It fires the right-hand gun alone. In the game: press: Fire the right Spandau.
controls.context: Firing one gun at a time lets the pilot keep firing if the other gun jams.

controls.name: Control column
controls.text: This is the control stick (or control column). Moving it forward and back tilts the plane's nose down and up, moving it left and right rolls the plane. In the game: pitch: Pitch; roll: Roll.
controls.context: It is the pilot's main flight control. Everything else in the cockpit supports it.

panels.name: Throttle and left-hand controls
panels.text: These are the throttle levers and the other controls the pilot's left hand reaches on the left side.
panels.context: The pilot sets engine power, propeller, trim, flaps and gear with the left hand.

controls.name: Throttle lever on the column
controls.text: This is the throttle, the lever that makes the engine stronger or weaker, like the gas pedal of a car. In the game: axis: Engine power.
controls.context: The pilot works it with the left hand: forward for take-off and fighting, back for landing.

controls.name: Spark advance lever
controls.text: This small lever sets the ignition timing, when the engine's sparks are made. The catalog calls it the spark advance lever. In the game: axis: Ignition timing (spark advance).
controls.context: It sits in a small quadrant on the left of the cockpit.
